h: Your First Time on the Snow
p: Never been on skis before? You're in good company. Plenty of people at Snozone have never seen a ski lift in their lives, and a beginner lesson is the best way in. Instructors start on the gentle lower part of the slope, getting you comfortable standing, sliding and stopping before you go anywhere near the steeper bits.

Skis or a snowboard, boots and a helmet are usually provided as part of a lesson, but it's worth checking what's included when you book. What you'll need to bring is your own warm kit: a waterproof jacket and trousers, gloves, a hat or buff and thick socks. Jeans are a bad idea, as they soak through fast and stay cold. Indoor snow is kept below freezing, so layers you can take off later are better than one big coat.

Expect to fall over, especially on a board. That's normal, and part of why it's such a laugh with friends or family. Most people find their confidence grows quickly over a session or two, and by the time you're heading to the mountains you'll be glad you got the wobbly bits out of the way here.

Afterwards, you'll want something warm. Xscape has plenty of food options, and if you'd rather stretch your legs, the Grand Union Canal winds through Milton Keynes with towpaths for a gentle stroll. Families with younger children might also like Gulliver's Land, the family theme park in the city aimed at little ones, as a separate day out.
Book lessons well in advance before school holidays and the ski season, when they fill fastest.
